words.enDefinition: a pass allowing someone to attend a specific organised event

examples.en: My event ticket showed the match date but not the entrance.
examples.zh: 我的「活动门票」上有比赛日期，却没写入口。

examples.en: I bought an event ticket online for the university basketball game.
examples.zh: 我在网上买了张大学篮球赛的「活动门票」。

words.enDefinition: a ticket offered specifically to people eligible as students

examples.en: I got a student ticket for the match through the university website.
examples.zh: 我通过学校网站拿到了一张比赛的「学生门票」。

examples.en: The venue listed a student ticket alongside the standard adult ticket online.
examples.zh: 场馆在网上把「学生门票」和普通成人票列在一起。

words.enDefinition: the number of event tickets set aside for eligible students

examples.en: The student ticket allotment for the opening game ran out before my lecture.
examples.zh: 开场赛的「学生票配额」在我上课前就用完了。

examples.en: The university increased its student ticket allotment for the final day of competition.
examples.zh: 学校增加了最后一个比赛日的「学生票配额」。

words.enDefinition: to request and secure a ticket from an allocation for students

examples.en: I planned to claim a student ticket as soon as my lab session ended.
examples.zh: 我打算实验课一结束就「领取学生门票」。

examples.en: The email explained how to claim a student ticket for the next home game.
examples.zh: 邮件说明了下一场主场比赛如何「领取学生门票」。

collocations: claim a student ticket in advance
eligible to claim a student ticket

words.enDefinition: a pass allowing a student to bring a guest to an event

examples.en: I asked if a student guest pass was available for my flatmate.
examples.zh: 我问能不能给室友一张「学生访客票」。

examples.en: The student guest pass was listed separately in my athletics ticket account.
examples.zh: 「学生访客票」在我的校体育票务账户里单独列出。

words.enDefinition: a pass for eligible students covering multiple events in a season

examples.en: My roommate bought a student season pass because she goes to most games.
examples.zh: 室友买了张「学生赛季通票」，因为大部分比赛她都去看。

examples.en: We checked which sports the student season pass covered before making a decision.
examples.zh: 做决定前，我们查了这张「学生赛季通票」涵盖哪些体育项目。

words.enDefinition: a ticket for one game rather than multiple games

examples.en: I wanted a single-game ticket because my sister was visiting for one weekend.
examples.zh: 我想买张「单场比赛门票」，因为妹妹只来一个周末。

examples.en: The single-game ticket for Sunday's game was still available after class.
examples.zh: 下课后，周日比赛的「单场比赛门票」仍可购买。

words.enDefinition: a pass covering every session of a multi-session event

examples.en: Our parents bought an all-session pass because we competed on different days.
examples.zh: 因为我俩在不同的日子参赛，父母买了张「全场次通票」。

examples.en: The all-session pass included both the morning events and the evening final.
examples.zh: 「全场次通票」包括上午的各项赛事和晚上的决赛。

words.enDefinition: a ticket provided at no charge by an event organiser

examples.en: I received a complimentary ticket after volunteering at an earlier match.
examples.zh: 我在之前一场比赛当过志愿者，后来收到一张「赠票」。

examples.en: The organisers issued a complimentary ticket to each student performer that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，主办方给每位学生表演者发了一张「赠票」。

words.enDefinition: a ticket sold at the regular price without a discount

examples.en: My cousin bought a full-price ticket because she was no longer a student.
examples.zh: 表姐已经不是学生了，所以买了一张「全价门票」。

examples.en: The website showed that a full-price ticket included the same seats.
examples.zh: 网站显示，「全价门票」对应的座位也是一样的。

words.enDefinition: an admission category without a specific assigned individual seat

examples.en: Our general admission ticket let us choose any open seat within our section.
examples.zh: 这张票「入场不指定座位」，我们可以坐本区内任意空座。

examples.en: Our tickets said general admission, so there were no seat numbers.
examples.zh: 我们的票写着「入场不指定座位」，所以没有座位号。

words.enDefinition: a ticket that lets its holder watch from a standing area

examples.en: We chose a standing ticket because we wanted to stay near the stage.
examples.zh: 我们想离舞台近一点，就选了「站席票」。

examples.en: The standing ticket cost less than a seat on the upper level.
examples.zh: 「站席票」比上层看台的座票便宜。

words.enDefinition: the point when some or all event tickets become available

examples.en: My friend put the ticket release date in our shared calendar.
examples.zh: 朋友把「门票放出」日期加进了我们的共享日历。

examples.en: The club announced another ticket release after adding an extra seating section.
examples.zh: 增开一个座位区后，俱乐部宣布再「放出一批门票」。

words.enDefinition: an early ticket sale for a defined group before public sales

examples.en: The arts club announced a presale for its student members on Monday.
examples.zh: 艺术社周一宣布面向学生会员「预售」门票。

examples.en: I bought my seat during the presale before the general sale began.
examples.zh: 我在公开发售前的「预售」阶段买了座位。

words.enDefinition: a code permitting entry to a ticket sale before public access

examples.en: The email included a presale code for the campus arts series.
examples.zh: 邮件里有校园系列艺术活动的「预售资格码」。

examples.en: The presale code let me see which seats were in the early sale.
examples.zh: 用「预售资格码」后，我能看到预售范围内的座位。

words.enDefinition: the stage when tickets are available to the wider public

examples.en: The general sale began after the university members had their early access.
examples.zh: 学校会员享受优先购买后，门票开始「面向公众发售」。

examples.en: I waited for the general sale because I wasn't part of the club.
examples.zh: 我不是俱乐部成员，就等到「面向公众发售」再买。

words.enDefinition: the period when people can purchase tickets for an event

examples.en: The ticket sale window closed before I finished my seminar that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午我上完研讨课前，「门票销售时段」就结束了。

examples.en: The athletics department published the ticket sale window in its weekly newsletter.
examples.zh: 体育部在每周简报里公布了「门票销售时段」。

words.enDefinition: the maximum number of tickets one buyer can obtain

examples.en: The ticket limit for that event was shown before we selected seats.
examples.zh: 选座之前，页面显示了那场活动的「门票限购数量」。

examples.en: We checked the ticket limit before deciding how to book our seats.
examples.zh: 决定怎么订座前，我们查看了「门票限购数量」。

words.enDefinition: a system that randomly chooses who can receive or purchase tickets

examples.en: I entered the ticket lottery for a seat at the university final.
examples.zh: 我参加了大学决赛的「门票抽签」，想抽到一个座位。

examples.en: They held a ticket lottery because there were more interested students than seats.
examples.zh: 因为学生比座位多，所以采用了「门票抽签」。

collocations: hear back from a ticket lottery

words.enDefinition: a list of people who want tickets if any become available

examples.en: I joined the ticket waitlist after seeing that the first batch was gone.
examples.zh: 看到第一批票已经售完，我加入了「门票候补名单」。

examples.en: My place on the ticket waitlist changed the morning of the game.
examples.zh: 比赛当天上午，我在「门票候补名单」上的顺序变了。

words.enDefinition: a line of people waiting for space to become available

examples.en: My friends waited in the standby line outside the lecture hall for tickets.
examples.zh: 朋友们在讲堂外的「现场候补队伍」里等着有没有票。

examples.en: They moved the standby line indoors when the rain started that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上开始下雨，工作人员让「现场候补队伍」移到屋里。

words.enDefinition: an online area holding buyers before they enter a sale queue

examples.en: I opened the virtual waiting room before the match tickets went on sale.
examples.zh: 球赛门票开卖前，我打开了「线上等候室」。

examples.en: The virtual waiting room showed the start time for the next ticket sale.
examples.zh: 「线上等候室」显示了下一次门票销售的开始时间。

collocations: wait in a virtual waiting room

words.enDefinition: an online line that gives buyers turns to shop for tickets

examples.en: The ticketing queue opened when the school released more seats that week.
examples.zh: 学校那一周放出更多座位时，「购票等待队列」开始了。

examples.en: I left the ticketing queue once my classmate told me all seats were gone.
examples.zh: 同学说座位都没了，我就退出了「购票等待队列」。

words.enDefinition: a button label for opening available ticket options for an event

examples.en: I selected "Find tickets", then checked which dates had any seats left.
examples.zh: 我点了「查找门票」，再看哪些日期还有座位。

examples.en: The link said "Find tickets", but the ticket sale hadn't started yet.
examples.zh: 链接上写着「查找门票」，不过门票还没开卖。

words.enDefinition: to keep selected seats unavailable to others for a limited time

examples.en: The booking site could hold seats while I checked the date again.
examples.zh: 我重新核对日期时，订票网站可以「暂时锁定座位」。

examples.en: The salesperson offered to hold seats until I had found my card.
examples.zh: 售票员说可以「暂时锁定座位」，等我把卡找出来。

words.enDefinition: indicates that selected seats are no longer kept for the buyer

examples.en: The website showed "Seat hold expired", so the selected seats went back on sale.
examples.zh: 网站显示「座位暂留已超时」，选中的座位重新开放出售。

examples.en: I saw "Seat hold expired" after a long phone call interrupted my booking.
examples.zh: 一个长电话打断了订票过程，挂断后我看到了「座位暂留已超时」。

words.enDefinition: seats that are still available for a particular event

examples.en: I checked the remaining seats before asking whether my roommate could come.
examples.zh: 我查完「剩余座位」，才问室友能不能来。

examples.en: Most of the remaining seats were behind the team benches that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，多数「剩余座位」在球队替补席后面。

words.enDefinition: indicates that only a small number of tickets remain available

examples.en: The page said "Limited availability", so we looked at a different date.
examples.zh: 页面上说「余票有限」，我们就去看了另一个日期。

examples.en: An email marked the afternoon match as having limited availability this week.
examples.zh: 邮件注明，本周下午那场比赛「余票有限」。

words.enDefinition: an extra charge for arranging or processing a ticket booking

examples.en: The booking page added a booking fee before showing the total price.
examples.zh: 订票页面显示总价前，加上了「订票手续费」。

examples.en: We checked the booking fee before deciding which match to attend together.
examples.zh: 决定一起去看哪场比赛前，我们查了「订票手续费」。

words.enDefinition: a named or numbered group of seats within a venue

examples.en: The staff member pointed us toward the right seating section upstairs.
examples.zh: 工作人员指给我们楼上的正确「观众席分区」。

examples.en: The map used different colours for each seating section around the court.
examples.zh: 场馆地图用不同颜色标出球场周围的每个「观众席分区」。

words.enDefinition: a letter showing which row a particular seat is in

examples.en: I read the row letter twice because it looked like a number.
examples.zh: 那个「排号字母」看起来像数字，所以我看了两遍。

examples.en: The row letter was on the sign at the end of the aisle.
examples.zh: 过道尽头的牌子上写着「排号字母」。

words.enDefinition: an area at a venue set aside for student spectators

examples.en: I met my classmates in the student section before the match.
examples.zh: 比赛前，我在「学生看台」见到了同学。

examples.en: The student section was on the same level as the team benches.
examples.zh: 「学生看台」和球队替补席在同一层。

words.enDefinition: part of a venue intended for families attending an event

examples.en: We chose the family section when my friend's younger brother came along.
examples.zh: 朋友的弟弟也来时，我们选了「家庭观众区」。

examples.en: The family section was clearly marked on the map outside the arena.
examples.zh: 体育馆外的地图清楚标出了「家庭观众区」。

words.enDefinition: the area set aside for supporters of the host team

examples.en: My roommate found us seats in the home supporters' section for Saturday's match.
examples.zh: 室友给我们在「主队球迷区」找到了周六比赛的座位。

examples.en: The home supporters' section started singing when the players walked onto the field.
examples.zh: 球员走上球场时，「主队球迷区」的人开始唱歌。

collocations: sit in the home supporters' section
tickets for the home supporters' section

words.enDefinition: the area reserved for people supporting the visiting team

examples.en: My cousin asked where the away supporters' section was before buying her ticket.
examples.zh: 表姐买票前问了「客队球迷区」在哪里。

examples.en: We could hear the away supporters' section from our seats near midfield.
examples.zh: 从靠近中场的座位上，我们能听到「客队球迷区」的声音。

collocations: sit in the away supporters' section
tickets for the away supporters' section

words.enDefinition: a large tiered structure for spectators beside a sports area

examples.en: A loud cheer came from the grandstand after the close finish.
examples.zh: 比赛临近结束、胜负难分时，「大型看台」上爆发出一阵欢呼。

examples.en: My friends watched from the grandstand rather than standing by the track.
examples.zh: 朋友没站在跑道边，而是在「大型看台」上观看。

words.enDefinition: rows of raised benches for spectators, especially in North America

examples.en: We sat on the bleachers behind the school baseball field.
examples.zh: 我们坐在学校棒球场后面的「阶梯式长凳看台」上。

examples.en: The metal bleachers felt cold by the second half of the match.
examples.zh: 比赛进行到下半场时，金属的「阶梯式长凳看台」摸起来已经很凉。

words.enDefinition: a tiered spectator area with space to stand instead of seats

examples.en: We watched the match from a standing terrace near one corner.
examples.zh: 我们站在靠近一个角落的「阶梯式站席看台」上看比赛。

examples.en: The standing terrace was clearly marked on the stadium seating plan.
examples.zh: 体育场座位图上清楚标出了「阶梯式站席看台」。

words.enDefinition: the lower group of seating tiers around an arena or stadium

examples.en: Our tickets were for the lower bowl near the team benches.
examples.zh: 我们的票在「下层环形看台」，靠近球队替补席。

examples.en: The students filled the lower bowl before the afternoon event began.
examples.zh: 下午的赛事开始前，学生们坐满了「下层环形看台」。

words.enDefinition: the higher group of seating tiers around an arena or stadium

examples.en: From the upper bowl, we could see both ends of the field.
examples.zh: 从「上层环形看台」能看到球场两端。

examples.en: The upper bowl slowly emptied while we waited for the stairs to clear.
examples.zh: 我们等着楼梯上的人走散时，「上层环形看台」渐渐空了。

collocations: head up to the upper bowl

words.enDefinition: informal term for seats very high and far from the action

examples.en: We bought nosebleed seats because we were on a student budget.
examples.zh: 学生手头紧，我们就买了「高处远座」。

examples.en: Even from the nosebleed seats, the court was easy to see.
examples.zh: 就算坐在「高处远座」，也能看清球场。

words.enDefinition: seats right beside the playing area of a sports court

examples.en: The courtside seats gave us a clear look at the players warming up.
examples.zh: 坐在「场边近座」，我们能清楚看到球员热身。

examples.en: My aunt had courtside seats when her university hosted the basketball tournament.
examples.zh: 姨妈的大学办篮球锦标赛时，她坐的是「场边近座」。

words.enDefinition: seats positioned beyond the goal at one end of the field

examples.en: Our seats behind the goal gave us a clear view of the players celebrating.
examples.zh: 坐在「球门后方座位」上，我们能清楚看到球员庆祝。

examples.en: My cousin chose seats behind the goal because she preferred that end of the stadium.
examples.zh: 表姐喜欢体育场那一端，所以选了「球门后方座位」。

collocations: watch from seats behind the goal

words.zhGloss: 带额外服务的高级座位
words.enDefinition: premium seats that may include access to special facilities or services
acceptedZhAnswers: 带额外服务的高级座位

examples.en: His parents had club seats near a lounge for ticket holders.
examples.zh: 他父母坐的是「带额外服务的高级座位」，附近有供持票人使用的休息室。

examples.en: The map showed where the club seats were in the new arena.
examples.zh: 地图上标出了新体育馆里「带额外服务的高级座位」的位置。

words.enDefinition: a private room at an event venue for watching and hosting guests

examples.en: The alumni group watched the match from a hospitality suite upstairs.
examples.zh: 校友小组在楼上的「场馆贵宾包厢」看了比赛。

examples.en: Our department used a hospitality suite for a small group of guests.
examples.zh: 我们系安排一小群客人在「场馆贵宾包厢」观赛。

words.enDefinition: seating designed for people with disabilities or other access needs

examples.en: I asked about accessible seating before booking tickets for our group.
examples.zh: 给我们这组人订票前，我问了问「无障碍座席」的情况。

examples.en: The arena showed its accessible seating on a separate section map.
examples.zh: 体育馆用一张单独的分区图标出了「无障碍座席」。

words.enDefinition: a seat for someone accompanying a person using accessible seating

examples.en: I asked whether my companion seat was next to the wheelchair space.
examples.zh: 我问自己的「陪同人员座位」是不是挨着轮椅观赛位。

examples.en: A companion seat was marked beside each accessible spot on the map.
examples.zh: 地图在每个无障碍位置旁都标出了「陪同人员座位」。

words.enDefinition: a view that lets spectators see the activity without obstructions

examples.en: The seat behind the railing still had a clear sightline to the court.
examples.zh: 栏杆后的座位看球场仍然有「无遮挡视线」。

examples.en: I wanted a clear sightline because it was my first live game.
examples.zh: 这是我第一次到现场看球，我想选个「无遮挡视线」的座位。

collocations: find a seat with a clear sightline

words.enDefinition: a seat from which some of the show is blocked

examples.en: I decided against an obstructed-view seat because of a pillar nearby.
examples.zh: 附近有根柱子，我最后没买「视线受阻座位」。

examples.en: The ticket office marked one corner seat as an obstructed-view seat.
examples.zh: 售票处把角落的一个座位标成「视线受阻座位」。

words.enDefinition: the scene visible from one particular seat at a venue

examples.en: The website showed the view from your seat before you confirmed the booking.
examples.zh: 你确认订票之前，网站会显示「从座位看到的视野」。

examples.en: I wanted to see the view from your seat before deciding on that row.
examples.zh: 我想先看看「从座位看到的视野」，再决定选不选那一排。

collocations: check the view from your seat
preview the view from your seat
picture of the view from your seat

words.enDefinition: seating under a roof that protects spectators from the weather

examples.en: We chose covered seating after seeing clouds above the stadium that morning.
examples.zh: 早上看到体育场上方积云，我们就选了「有顶棚的座席」。

examples.en: The covered seating filled quickly when it started raining after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭后开始下雨，「有顶棚的座席」很快就坐满了。

words.enDefinition: the seat at either end of a row of seats

examples.en: I chose an end seat so it would be easier to leave.
examples.zh: 我选了「一排最边上的座位」，这样离开时更方便。

examples.en: The only available end seat was in the second row of our section.
examples.zh: 唯一剩下的「一排最边上的座位」在那个区的第二排。

words.enDefinition: a place at a venue where tickets are sold or collected

examples.en: We went to the box office before the evening basketball game.
examples.zh: 晚上篮球赛前，我们去了「场馆售票处」。

examples.en: My friend checked whether the box office could print her ticket there.
examples.zh: 朋友问「场馆售票处」能不能现场把她的票打印出来。

collocations: collect tickets from the box office

words.enDefinition: a ticket arrangement where booked tickets are collected at the venue

examples.en: I selected will call because I wanted to collect our tickets in person.
examples.zh: 我选择「现场领预订票」，因为想亲自把我们的票领到手。

examples.en: A sign pointed from the main entrance to the will call area.
examples.zh: 有块牌子从正门指向「现场领预订票」的区域。

words.enDefinition: a ticket counter where customers collect tickets already booked

examples.en: I found the will-call window next to the main ticket sales office.
examples.zh: 我在主售票处旁边找到了「预订票现场领取窗口」。

examples.en: The will-call window closed before the last event started that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚最后一场赛事开始前，「预订票现场领取窗口」就关闭了。

collocations: line up at the will-call window

words.enDefinition: a message confirming arrangements to collect tickets from a venue

examples.en: I saved the ticket pickup confirmation to check which counter we should visit.
examples.zh: 我保存了「领票确认信息」，想确认该去哪个柜台。

examples.en: The ticket pickup confirmation arrived in the same email as the match details.
examples.zh: 「领票确认信息」和比赛详情在同一封邮件里发来。

words.enDefinition: evidence that a person qualifies for a particular ticket or benefit

examples.en: The ticket office asked for proof of eligibility before issuing the student pass.
examples.zh: 售票处先要看「资格证明」，再发学生通票。

examples.en: A student card was listed as acceptable proof of eligibility for that event.
examples.zh: 那场活动明确列出，学生证可以作为「资格证明」。

words.enDefinition: the sale of tickets on the day an event takes place

examples.en: The arena offered event-day ticket sales for the final match on Saturday.
examples.zh: 周六的决赛，体育馆提供「活动当天售票」。

examples.en: A notice said event-day ticket sales were only available at the main entrance.
examples.zh: 告示写着，「活动当天售票」只在主入口办理。

collocations: event-day ticket sales at the venue

words.enDefinition: a message indicating that tickets for an event are not available to access or buy at the moment

examples.en: The app displayed "Tickets not yet available," although the booking had already been confirmed.
examples.zh: 虽然订票已确认，但应用显示「门票暂不可查看」。

examples.en: We saw "Tickets not yet available" when we opened the booking page after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭后打开订票页面时，我们看到了「门票暂不可查看」。

collocations: notice reading tickets not yet available

words.enDefinition: an account button that opens the tickets linked to the booking

examples.en: I selected "View my tickets" to find the row listed in my booking.
examples.zh: 我点了「查看我的门票」，查看订票记录里的排号。

examples.en: The confirmation email linked to "View my tickets" underneath the event description.
examples.zh: 确认邮件在活动介绍下方放了「查看我的门票」的链接。

words.enDefinition: a code on a ticket that can be scanned for entry

examples.en: The attendant asked me to display the ticket barcode on my phone.
examples.zh: 入场工作人员请我在手机上显示「门票条码」。

examples.en: I could see the seat details above the ticket barcode in the app.
examples.zh: 我能在应用里的「门票条码」上方看到座位详情。

words.enDefinition: to read a ticket with a device to check it

examples.en: The volunteer pointed to the reader and said, "Please scan your ticket here."
examples.zh: 志愿者指着扫码器说：「请在这里扫描你的门票」。

examples.en: The sign reminded everyone to scan your ticket before going through the gate.
examples.zh: 告示提醒大家过闸口前「扫描自己的门票」。

collocations: ask someone to scan your ticket
scan your ticket at the gate

words.enDefinition: a device that reads and checks event tickets at entry

examples.en: The volunteer raised a ticket scanner when we reached the front.
examples.zh: 我们排到前面时，志愿者举起了「门票扫描设备」。

examples.en: A ticket scanner beeped every time a ticket was read correctly.
examples.zh: 每次正确读取一张票，「门票扫描设备」都会发出一声提示音。

words.enDefinition: says that a reader is not successfully reading a ticket

examples.en: The attendant said, "Your ticket won't scan," and asked me to wait.
examples.zh: 工作人员说：「你的门票扫不出来」，请我等一下。

examples.en: I told the gate attendant, "My ticket won't scan on this screen."
examples.zh: 我告诉入口工作人员：「我的门票扫不出来」，用的是这个界面。

collocations: tell staff your ticket won't scan
ask why the ticket won't scan
alert saying the ticket won't scan

words.enDefinition: a message that a ticket has previously been scanned for admission

examples.en: The reader showed "Ticket already scanned," and the attendant took another look.
examples.zh: 扫码器显示「门票已扫验」，工作人员又看了一遍。

examples.en: I asked the ticket desk about the "Ticket already scanned" message on my screen.
examples.zh: 我向票务服务台询问手机屏幕上的「门票已扫验」提示。

words.enDefinition: the part of a printed ticket kept after it is checked

examples.en: I saved the ticket stub from my first game at university.
examples.zh: 我留了第一次在大学看球赛的「票根」。

examples.en: My dad found a ticket stub in an old photo album.
examples.zh: 爸爸在一本旧相册里找到一张「票根」。

words.enDefinition: the authorised process of sending an electronic ticket to another person

examples.en: The box office confirmed that a ticket transfer was available for this event.
examples.zh: 售票处确认这场活动允许「门票转交」。

examples.en: I received a ticket transfer from my roommate before the game.
examples.zh: 比赛前，我收到了室友发来的「门票转交」请求。

words.enDefinition: to confirm that you want to receive a ticket sent to you

examples.en: My friend asked me to accept the transfer before we left for the match.
examples.zh: 朋友让我在出发看比赛前「接受门票转交」。

examples.en: The app let me read the event details before I could accept the transfer.
examples.zh: 在我「接受门票转交」前，应用先让我查看活动详情。

collocations: ask someone to accept the transfer

words.enDefinition: indicates that a ticket transfer has not yet been completed

examples.en: The app showed "Transfer pending" while my friend checked her email.
examples.zh: 朋友查看邮件时，应用显示「门票转交待确认」。

examples.en: I saw "Transfer pending" underneath the ticket I had sent that morning.
examples.zh: 那天早上我发出门票后，看见票下方写着「门票转交待确认」。

words.enDefinition: a ticket that may only be used by the original holder

examples.en: My student pass showed that it was a non-transferable ticket for that match.
examples.zh: 我的学生通票显示，这一场对应的是「不可转交门票」。

examples.en: The portal marked one option as a non-transferable ticket before checkout.
examples.zh: 结账前，网站把一个选项注明为「不可转交门票」。

collocations: check whether it is a non-transferable ticket

words.enDefinition: a schedule label for the time a venue starts admitting people

examples.en: The notice said "Gates open at noon" for the afternoon match.
examples.zh: 下午那场比赛的告示写着「中午开放场馆入口」。

examples.en: I found the line marked "Gates open" in the event email.
examples.zh: 我在活动邮件里找到了标着「开放场馆入口」的一行。

words.enDefinition: an entry point specifically designated for students attending an event

examples.en: We followed the signs to the student entrance behind the gym.
examples.zh: 我们跟着标牌走到体育馆后面的「学生专用入口」。

examples.en: My friend waited near the student entrance while I found our tickets.
examples.zh: 我找票时，朋友在「学生专用入口」附近等着。

words.enDefinition: someone responsible for helping or checking people at an entry gate

examples.en: The gate attendant read my ticket and pointed us toward the stairs.
examples.zh: 「入口工作人员」看了我的票，给我们指了楼梯的方向。

examples.en: A gate attendant pointed out the sign for the student entrance.
examples.zh: 一位「入口工作人员」给我指了学生专用入口的标牌。

words.enDefinition: a marked passage through which people enter a venue

examples.en: The staff opened a second entry lane when the crowd grew.
examples.zh: 人越来越多时，工作人员开了第二条「入场通道」。

examples.en: I joined the wrong entry lane and asked a volunteer for directions.
examples.zh: 我排错了「入场通道」，就找志愿者问路。

words.enDefinition: an examination of bags before people may enter an event

examples.en: There was a bag check before people reached the ticket scanners.
examples.zh: 人们到门票扫码处之前，要先经过「入场验包」。

examples.en: The bag check moved quickly while we waited outside the stadium.
examples.zh: 我们在体育场外排队时，「入场验包」进行得很快。

words.enDefinition: venue rules requiring some or all bags to be transparent

examples.en: The stadium's website explained its clear bag policy before the student game.
examples.zh: 球赛前，体育场网站说明了它的「入场透明包规定」。

examples.en: My friend had a question about the clear bag policy at that venue.
examples.zh: 朋友对那个场馆的「入场透明包规定」有个问题。

words.enDefinition: a list of things that may not enter a venue

examples.en: The arena displayed a prohibited items list near the line for tickets.
examples.zh: 体育馆在排队买票的地方附近展示了「禁止携带物品清单」。

examples.en: I looked up the prohibited items list before leaving for the festival.
examples.zh: 出发去参加节庆活动前，我查了「禁止携带物品清单」。

words.enDefinition: a notice saying people cannot enter again after leaving

examples.en: The sign said "No re-entry," so we stayed inside during the break.
examples.zh: 标牌写着「离场后不得再入场」，所以休息时我们留在里面。

examples.en: The printed ticket showed "No re-entry" just below the event name.
examples.zh: 纸质门票在活动名称下面写着「离场后不得再入场」。

collocations: venue with a no re-entry rule

words.enDefinition: an ink mark showing that a visitor may enter again

examples.en: The volunteer offered a re-entry stamp when we stepped outside briefly.
examples.zh: 我们短暂出去时，志愿者提出给我们盖个「再次入场用的印章」。

examples.en: My re-entry stamp was still visible when I returned to the venue.
examples.zh: 我回到场馆时，「再次入场用的印章」还清晰可见。

words.enDefinition: a credential permitting entry to the playing area at a venue

examples.en: The student photographer had a field pass for the university game.
examples.zh: 拍校队比赛的学生有一张「赛场通行证」。

examples.en: Our volunteer supervisor checked the field pass before letting Mark through.
examples.zh: 志愿者负责人核查了「赛场通行证」，才让马克通过。

words.enDefinition: a credential that grants journalists access to designated event areas

examples.en: The student newspaper sent a reporter with a press pass that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上，学生报派了一名持「媒体通行证」的记者。

examples.en: The volunteer explained where the press pass could be used at the venue.
examples.zh: 志愿者解释了「媒体通行证」能在场馆的哪些地方使用。

words.enDefinition: a staff member who helps people find their seats

examples.en: An usher showed us the steps to our seating section.
examples.zh: 一位「引座员」指给我们通往座位分区的楼梯。

examples.en: My coursemate volunteered as an usher at the evening match.
examples.zh: 同专业同学在晚上那场比赛做志愿「引座员」。

words.enDefinition: the main public walkway linking areas inside a large venue

examples.en: I met my roommate on the main concourse near the stairs.
examples.zh: 我在楼梯附近的「场馆主通道」上见到了室友。

examples.en: The main concourse linked our seating area to the opposite entrance.
examples.zh: 「场馆主通道」把我们的座位区和对面的入口连了起来。

words.enDefinition: a small outlet selling snacks and drinks to people at events

examples.en: We stopped at a concession stand for water before finding our seats.
examples.zh: 找座位之前，我们先去「场馆餐饮售卖摊」买了水。

examples.en: The concession stand by our section closed just after the final whistle.
examples.zh: 终场哨响后没多久，我们观众区旁的「场馆餐饮售卖摊」就关了。

words.enDefinition: a counter where event visitors can get information or help

examples.en: The volunteer sent us to the guest services desk for a venue map.
examples.zh: 志愿者让我们到「观众服务台」拿场馆地图。

examples.en: The guest services desk was near the end of the main walkway.
examples.zh: 「观众服务台」靠近主通道的尽头。

collocations: ask at the guest services desk

words.enDefinition: a display showing the current score at a sports event

examples.en: The scoreboard was hard to read from the upper seating section.
examples.zh: 从上层座席很难看清「现场记分牌」。

examples.en: We looked at the scoreboard before heading back to our seats.
examples.zh: 回座位前，我们看了一眼「现场记分牌」。

words.enDefinition: a large screen used to show video inside a venue

examples.en: I missed the play but saw it on the video board.
examples.zh: 那个回合我没看见，不过在「场馆视频大屏」上补看了。

examples.en: The video board showed the performers before they came onto the field.
examples.zh: 表演者走上赛场前，「场馆视频大屏」先显示了他们的画面。

words.enDefinition: a spoken announcement broadcast over a venue's loudspeakers

examples.en: A public address announcement reminded us where to find the student exit.
examples.zh: 一则「场馆广播通知」提醒我们去哪里找学生出口。

examples.en: We stopped talking when the public address announcement asked people to listen.
examples.zh: 「场馆广播通知」请大家注意听时，我们就不说话了。

collocations: listen for a public address announcement

words.enDefinition: the person who gives spoken updates over the venue's loudspeakers

examples.en: The PA announcer welcomed the visiting team before the players warmed up.
examples.zh: 球员热身前，「现场广播员」向客队表示欢迎。

examples.en: My classmate worked as the PA announcer for a campus volleyball match.
examples.zh: 同学在一场校园排球比赛上担任「现场广播员」。

words.enDefinition: a performance presented during the break halfway through a sports game

examples.en: We stayed in our seats to watch the marching band's halftime show.
examples.zh: 我们留在座位上，看行进乐队的「中场表演」。

examples.en: My coursemate performed in the halftime show at our first home game.
examples.zh: 同专业同学参加了我们第一场主场比赛的「中场表演」。

words.enDefinition: spectators mainly supporting the team playing at its own venue

examples.en: The home crowd got louder when the players returned to the court.
examples.zh: 球员回到球场时，「主场观众」的声音更大了。

examples.en: I was surprised by how early the home crowd filled the stands.
examples.zh: 「主场观众」很早就坐满了看台，我挺意外。

words.enDefinition: fans who travel to support their team at an away event

examples.en: The travelling supporters started a chant near the far end of the stadium.
examples.zh: 体育场远端附近，「随队出行的球迷」带头喊起了口号。

examples.en: We met two travelling supporters on the train after the match.
examples.zh: 赛后我们在火车上认识了两位「随队出行的球迷」。

words.zhGloss: 不偏向任何一队的观众
words.enDefinition: someone watching a game without supporting either particular team
acceptedZhAnswers: 不偏向任何一队的观众

examples.en: I went as a neutral spectator because neither team was from my school.
examples.zh: 两队都不是我们学校的，所以我作为「不偏向任何一队的观众」去看了比赛。

examples.en: As a neutral spectator, I enjoyed listening to fans from both sides.
examples.zh: 作为「不偏向任何一队的观众」，我喜欢听两边球迷助威。

collocations: enjoy a match as a neutral spectator

words.enDefinition: someone who has a pass for a set of seasonal games

examples.en: My neighbour is a season-ticket holder and knows everyone in her row.
examples.zh: 邻居是「赛季通票持有人」，认识她那一排的所有人。

examples.en: A season-ticket holder showed me the fastest route to the upper seats.
examples.zh: 一位「赛季通票持有人」给我指了去上层座位最近的路。

words.enDefinition: an audience at an event for which all tickets were sold

examples.en: The final drew a sellout crowd even though it was a weekday.
examples.zh: 虽然是工作日，决赛还是吸引了「满座的观众」。

examples.en: I had never heard a sellout crowd cheer inside such a small arena.
examples.zh: 我从没在这么小的体育馆里听过「满座的观众」一起欢呼。

words.enDefinition: a reported number of people who attended a particular event

examples.en: The attendance figure appeared on screen just before the game ended.
examples.zh: 比赛结束前不久，屏幕上显示了「到场人数统计」。

examples.en: The student newspaper checked the attendance figure before publishing its article.
examples.zh: 学生报发稿前核实了「到场人数统计」。

words.enDefinition: to encourage participants while watching from a spectator area

examples.en: My classmates stayed to cheer from the stands until the final race ended.
examples.zh: 同学们留下来「在看台上欢呼助威」，直到最后一场比赛结束。

examples.en: I couldn't play, but I was happy to cheer from the stands that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午我不能上场，但很乐意「在看台上欢呼助威」。

collocations: come and cheer from the stands
stay to cheer from the stands
want to cheer from the stands

words.enDefinition: words or short lines jointly repeated by fans at an event

examples.en: I learned the words of a fan chant at my first game.
examples.zh: 第一次看比赛，我学会了一个「球迷助威口号」怎么喊。

examples.en: A fan chant spread through the section after the players came out.
examples.zh: 球员出场后，一个「球迷助威口号」传遍了整个看台区。

words.enDefinition: a very loud sound made by many spectators at once

examples.en: I could hear the roar of the crowd from outside the arena doors.
examples.zh: 站在体育馆门外也能听到「观众席的欢呼声」。

examples.en: It was hard to speak over the roar of the crowd after that moment.
examples.zh: 那一刻过后，「观众席的欢呼声」大得让人很难听清说话。

collocations: hear the roar of the crowd
over the roar of the crowd
drowned out by the roar of the crowd

words.enDefinition: strong excitement shared by everyone at an event

examples.en: Students created an electric atmosphere before the first home game even began.
examples.zh: 第一场主场比赛还没开始，学生们就让「现场气氛热烈起来」。

examples.en: We felt the electric atmosphere as soon as we entered the arena.
examples.zh: 我们一进体育馆，就感到「现场气氛热烈」。

words.expression: on the edge of your seat
words.lemma: on the edge of your seat
words.enDefinition: feeling intensely excited and eager to know what will happen
acceptedEnVariants: on the edge of your seat

examples.en: A close match can keep you on the edge of your seat until the last second.
examples.zh: 比分接近的比赛能让你一直「紧张得坐不住」，直到最后一秒。

examples.en: The last race had you on the edge of your seat even if you supported neither runner.
examples.zh: 最后一场赛跑就算两边你都不支持，也会让你「紧张得坐不住」。

collocations: keep you on the edge of your seat
leave you on the edge of your seat
have you on the edge of your seat

words.zhGloss: 穿上应援球队的代表色
words.enDefinition: to dress in colours associated with the team you support
acceptedZhAnswers: 穿上应援球队的代表色

examples.en: You could wear your team colours without buying anything from the stadium shop.
examples.zh: 不用在体育场商店买东西，也能「穿上应援球队的代表色」。

examples.en: The club poster said to wear your team colours for the final home match.
examples.zh: 俱乐部海报请大家在最后一场主场比赛时「穿上应援球队的代表色」。

collocations: decide to wear your team colours
remember to wear your team colours
invite fans to wear your team colours

words.enDefinition: a scarf displaying the colours or emblem of a sports team

examples.en: She waved her team scarf when the players walked out together.
examples.zh: 球员一起出场时，她挥了挥「球队应援围巾」。

examples.en: I borrowed a team scarf because my coat wasn't warm enough.
examples.zh: 我的外套不够暖和，就借了一条「球队应援围巾」。

words.enDefinition: a fan version of the shirt worn by a team's players

examples.en: My roommate wore a replica jersey over two sweaters at the match.
examples.zh: 室友那场比赛穿了两件毛衣，外面套了件「球迷版队服」。

examples.en: I recognised my cousin by the bright blue replica jersey she wore.
examples.zh: 我凭表姐那件亮蓝色的「球迷版队服」认出了她。

words.enDefinition: an area set up for sports fans to gather and socialise

examples.en: We met in the fan zone before walking over to the stadium.
examples.zh: 我们先在「球迷活动区」碰面，再走到体育场。

examples.en: The fan zone had a large screen and some tables for students.
examples.zh: 「球迷活动区」有块大屏幕，还给学生摆了些桌子。

words.enDefinition: a camera feed that shows spectators on a venue screen

examples.en: My brother waved when the fan cam showed him on the screen.
examples.zh: 「看台观众镜头」把我哥哥的画面放到大屏上时，他挥了挥手。

examples.en: We laughed when our classmates appeared on the fan cam together.
examples.zh: 同学们一起出现在「看台观众镜头」里时，我们笑了起来。

words.enDefinition: a booklet with information about a particular match and its participants

examples.en: The matchday programme listed all the players and described the half-time entertainment.
examples.zh: 「比赛日导览册」列出了所有球员，还介绍了中场的娱乐节目。

examples.en: I kept the matchday programme from my first match at that stadium.
examples.zh: 我留着第一次去那个体育场看比赛时的「比赛日导览册」。

words.enDefinition: a public statement identifying who will take part in the game

examples.en: We were still buying water when the lineup announcement began inside.
examples.zh: 我们还在买水，里面就开始了「参赛阵容播报」。

examples.en: The crowd listened closely to the lineup announcement just before the match.
examples.zh: 比赛快开始时，观众认真听着「参赛阵容播报」。

words.enDefinition: a recording of a recent moment shown again during an event

examples.en: We saw an instant replay and finally understood why everyone had cheered.
examples.zh: 看过「即时回放」后，我们终于明白大家为什么欢呼。

examples.en: The screen showed an instant replay while the players were standing still.
examples.zh: 球员站着不动时，大屏显示了「即时回放」。

collocations: see an instant replay on the screen

words.enDefinition: an encouragement for the audience to cheer loudly

examples.en: The announcer shouted "Make some noise!" and the student section immediately joined in.
examples.zh: 广播员喊了声「大家欢呼起来」，学生看台立刻响应。

examples.en: A banner said "Make some noise" as the visiting performers reached the field.
examples.zh: 客场表演队走上赛场时，一幅横幅写着「大家欢呼起来」。

collocations: ask fans to make some noise
make some noise for the team

words.enDefinition: asks an audience to applaud or cheer for a particular person

examples.en: The announcer said "Give it up for the volunteers" just before the last match.
examples.zh: 最后一场比赛开始前，广播员说：「请为志愿者鼓掌」。

examples.en: We heard "Give it up for our dancers" over the speakers at halftime.
examples.zh: 中场休息时扩音器里传来「请为我们的舞者鼓掌」。

collocations: give it up for the performers
please give it up for the band
give it up for our volunteers

words.enDefinition: entertainment presented to spectators before the start of a sports game

examples.en: We arrived early enough to see the whole pre-game show from our seats.
examples.zh: 我们到得早，坐在座位上看完了整场「赛前表演」。

examples.en: My friend volunteered to help with the pre-game show on Saturday.
examples.zh: 朋友报名在周六的「赛前表演」帮忙。

words.enDefinition: a public ceremony in which a winner receives a trophy

examples.en: Most of the students stayed for the trophy presentation after the game.
examples.zh: 比赛结束后，大部分同学留下来看了「奖杯颁发仪式」。

examples.en: I took a photo of our team at the trophy presentation.
examples.zh: 在「奖杯颁发仪式」上，我给我们队拍了张照片。

collocations: take part in the trophy presentation

words.enDefinition: to remain at a game until the referee ends it

examples.en: We chose to stay until the final whistle because the score was still close.
examples.zh: 因为比分咬得很紧，我们决定「待到终场哨响」。

examples.en: My roommate wanted to stay until the final whistle even though it was cold.
examples.zh: 虽然天冷，室友还是想「待到终场哨响」。

collocations: want to stay until the final whistle
decide to stay until the final whistle
plan to stay until the final whistle

words.enDefinition: a temporary interruption or postponement at an event because of rain

examples.en: We bought something warm to drink during the rain delay that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午比赛「因雨推迟」期间，我们买了点热饮。

examples.en: The announcer explained the rain delay before giving another start time.
examples.zh: 广播员先解释了「因雨推迟」，随后公布了另一个开始时间。

words.enDefinition: a notice saying that a game has been stopped temporarily

examples.en: The board read "Game suspended" while the officials looked at the field.
examples.zh: 裁判查看球场时，显示屏上写着「比赛暂时中止」。

examples.en: We saw "Game suspended" and waited for the next announcement together.
examples.zh: 看到「比赛暂时中止」后，我们一起等下一次广播。

words.enDefinition: exchanging a voucher or other entitlement for an actual event ticket

examples.en: The instructions for ticket redemption were printed below the student voucher.
examples.zh: 学生兑换券的下方印着「门票兑换」说明。

examples.en: I asked where ticket redemption took place before joining the wrong line.
examples.zh: 怕排错队，我先问了「门票兑换」在哪儿办理。

words.enDefinition: a voucher that can be exchanged for an event ticket

examples.en: My tutor handed me a ticket voucher for a campus wrestling match.
examples.zh: 老师给了我一张校园摔跤赛的「门票兑换券」。

examples.en: I checked whether the ticket voucher covered more than one event.
examples.zh: 我查了一下那张「门票兑换券」能不能用在不止一场活动里。

words.enDefinition: a website where eligible students can manage their event tickets

examples.en: The student ticket portal listed both the basketball game and the swim meet.
examples.zh: 「学生票务平台」上既列了篮球赛，也列了游泳比赛。

examples.en: I checked the student ticket portal for the latest date and venue information.
examples.zh: 我在「学生票务平台」上查看了最新的日期和场馆信息。

collocations: list events in the student ticket portal

words.enDefinition: a ticket valid on one day of a multi-day event

examples.en: I bought a single-day ticket because I was only free on Sunday.
examples.zh: 我只有周日有空，所以买了张「单日门票」。

examples.en: The single-day ticket covered every race on the selected day of competition.
examples.zh: 「单日门票」涵盖所选比赛日的每场赛跑。

words.enDefinition: a raised viewing area designed for spectators using wheelchairs

examples.en: The wheelchair viewing platform gave my friend a good view above the crowd.
examples.zh: 在「轮椅观赛平台」上，朋友能越过人群看得很清楚。

examples.en: The event map showed an entrance to the wheelchair viewing platform near us.
examples.zh: 活动地图标出了我们附近的一个「轮椅观赛平台」入口。

collocations: look for a wheelchair viewing platform

words.enDefinition: a diagram showing the numbered areas within a sports stadium

examples.en: I used the stadium section map to find the entrance closest to my seats.
examples.zh: 我用「体育场分区图」找离座位最近的入口。

examples.en: The stadium section map showed the student area on the side nearest campus.
examples.zh: 「体育场分区图」显示学生区在靠近校园的那一侧。

collocations: look at a stadium section map

words.enDefinition: a public walkway serving the higher levels of a venue

examples.en: We waited for our classmates on the upper concourse near the stairs.
examples.zh: 我们在楼梯附近的「场馆上层通道」等同学。

examples.en: The sign at the top of the ramp said "Upper concourse."
examples.zh: 坡道顶端的标牌写着「场馆上层通道」。

words.enDefinition: a set of tickets sold together as one purchase

examples.en: The ticket bundle covered three home games in the same month.
examples.zh: 这套「组合门票」涵盖同一个月的三场主场比赛。

examples.en: My roommate bought a ticket bundle that also included the final.
examples.zh: 室友买了一套「组合门票」，还包括决赛。

words.enDefinition: a sign or label identifying a row of seats

examples.en: The row marker was hard to read from the bottom of the steps.
examples.zh: 站在台阶下，很难看清「座位排号标识」。

examples.en: We checked the row marker before asking the usher to help us.
examples.zh: 我们先核对了「座位排号标识」，再请引座员帮忙。
